t.1.26.1: Then, having spent that night there, the greatly renowned Viśvāmitra smiled and spoke to Rāghava words of sweet syllables.
t.1.26.2: I am well pleased; may good fortune be yours, O greatly renowned prince! Filled with the highest affection, I give you weapons of every kind.
t.1.26.3: With these, overpowering your enemies in battle and bringing them under your control, you will conquer even the hosts of gods and asuras, together with the gandharvas and serpents.
t.1.26.4: Blessings upon you! I give you all those divine weapons in their entirety; the great divine Daṇḍacakra I shall give you, O Rāghava.
t.1.26.5: Then, O hero, I give you the discus of Dharma and likewise the discus of Kāla, the exceedingly fierce discus of Viṣṇu, and likewise the discus of Indra.
t.1.26.6: The Vajra weapon, O best of men, and likewise Śiva's excellent trident; the weapon Brahmaśiras as well, and also the Aiṣīka, O Rāghava.
t.1.26.7: O mighty-armed one, I give you the supreme Brāhma weapon, and also two maces, O Kākutstha, both of them, Modakī and Śikharī.
t.1.26.8: O Rāma, tiger among men, son of the king, I bestow upon you the two blazing ones: the noose of Dharma and likewise the noose of Kāla.
t.1.26.9: I give you the unsurpassed noose of Varuṇa as a weapon, and I bestow upon you two thunderbolts, the Dry and the Wet, O Raghunandana.
t.1.26.10: I give you the Paināka missile, and likewise the Nārāyaṇa missile, and the beloved Āgneya missile, known by the name of Śikhara.
t.1.26.11: First, O Rāghava, I give you the missile called Vāyavya, and the missile named Hayaśiras, and likewise the Krauñca missile as well.
t.1.26.12: And I give you a pair of spears, O sinless Kākutstha, and the dreadful club Kaṅkāla, and then the Kāpāla and the Kaṅkaṇa.
t.1.26.13: Those weapons which the asuras wield, I give all of these to you entirely, and also the great Vaidyādhara missile, called Nandana by name.
t.1.26.15: I give you, O Rāghava, the Prasvāpana and the Praśamana, and the Saura as well, the Darpaṇa and the Śoṣaṇa, and also the Saṃtāpana and the Vilāpana.
t.1.26.14: O mighty-armed son of the best of men, I give you the jewel among swords, and also the beloved Gāndharva missile, the one called Mānava by name.
t.1.26.16: Receive also the irresistible Madana, and likewise the weapon dear to Kandarpa, and the beloved Paiśāca missile known by the name Mohana, O tiger among men, O prince of great renown.
t.1.26.17: O tiger among men, the Tāmasa and the mighty Saumana, the invincible Saṃvarta and the Mausala, O son of a king.
t.1.26.18: O mighty-armed one, take the Satya missile, and likewise the supreme Māyādhara, and the terrible one called Tejaḥprabha, which draws away the energy of others.
t.1.26.19: The Soma missile named Śiśira, Tvaṣṭṛ's missile Sudāmana, the dreadful Śīteṣu of Bhaga as well, and then the Mānava.
t.1.26.20: O mighty-armed one, take these at once, O son of the king: these most noble weapons of great power, able to assume any form at will.
t.1.26.22: While the wise sage Viśvāmitra was chanting, all the most precious weapons presented themselves before Rāghava.
t.1.26.21: Then, standing with his face turned to the east, pure and moved by protective care, he, greatly pleased, gave Rāma the unsurpassed collection of mantras.
t.1.26.23: Then all of them, delighted, with joined palms, said to Rāma: “Here we are, O most noble Rāghava, your servants.”
t.1.26.24: Kākutstha accepted them and, touching them with his hand, urged them, saying, "You shall come to me whenever I call you to mind."
t.1.26.25: Then Rāma, glad at heart and of great splendour, saluted the great sage Viśvāmitra and made ready to depart.
